task.title: Create finite recurrence definitions through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/869 by exposing explicit writable creation of validated finite recurrence definitions.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity, goal, positive interval, and positive count before storage access, then validate the representable final instant in the kernel before appending a definition stream.
Persist through the existing kernel boundary and emit the exact deterministic recurrence JSON shape.
Fail closed on invalid, overflowing, or duplicate input without reading a clock, generating identity, persisting occurrences, dispatching, or executing.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because recurrence create was not recognized.
attempts.patch: Added creation, reopen, validation, overflow, duplicate, output, primitive pre-storage failure coverage, and kernel overflow no-stream coverage.

attempts.diagnostic: The durable kernel contract existed, but callers lacked a narrow command that preflighted primitive caller values before storage access and delegated derived range validation to the persistence boundary.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence create argument handling, typed primitive preflight validation, RecurrenceStore::create delegation with final-occurrence validation before append, shared JSON projection, diagnostics, and ADR-0042.

attempts.summary: Kept the write boundary behind the complete review gate.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit initially reported Review limit reached and later remained pending after one deliberate resume.
attempts.patch: Left auto-merge unarmed while review was pending and merged after exact-head Rust CI and CodeRabbit's recent-review summary covered base e22b5b5 through head 94cae1c with no actionable comments.

outcome.summary: The developer CLI can explicitly create one validated finite recurrence definition while leaving every occurrence and execution decision deferred.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0168-recurrence-creation-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 171 records: 171 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Validate primitive caller-owned values before opening a writable database, and validate derived final-occurrence representability in the kernel before append.
A creation adapter should reuse kernel persistence and the established response projection instead of duplicating invariants.
Definition creation grants only exact persistence authority, not occurrence lifecycle or execution authority.
A pending or rate-limited review cannot satisfy merge readiness.
